title: reduce auth ceremony: add credential-hydrator + stream-shuttle adapters (py/ts/go)
author: Priya Shah
ci_status: pass (one flaky integ test retried and passed)
release_notes: Introduces a cross-SDK Credential Hydrator that reduces auth handshake boilerplate and a lightweight Stream Shuttle adapter that enables pause/resume and typed envelopes. Bumps SDKs: python->2.18.0, typescript->1.27.0, go->1.8.0. No user-facing breaking changes; opt-in behavior behind feature flags for 30 days.
description: Background: Teams repeatedly reimplement credential prefetch/refresh and stream-resume glue in each SDK resulting in duplicated logic and subtle bugs during token swaps. Goal: provide a small, consistent primitive (Credential Hydrator) that centralizes TTL-aware prefetch/refresh and an orthogonal Stream Shuttle adapter to standardize minimal stream envelope metadata and pause/resume semantics across Py/TS/Go. Summary of changes: added a new auth primitive (Credential Hydrator) with a small public API: hydrate(ctx, key, ttl_hint) -> hydrated_token; added optional local prewarm caches and jittered refresh tasks; introduced Stream Shuttle (shuttle.{wrap,unwrap,checkpoint,resume}) which attaches a tiny typed header to stream frames to allow SDKs to implement pause/resume without changing user iteration patterns; implemented adapters in sdks/python, sdks/typescript, and sdks/go and wired into the existing session factories; added guided migration docs and examples; bump SDK versions. Why this design: hydrator centralizes token lifecycle (reduces double-refresh races), allows servers to prefer warmed delegated credentials, and provides observability hooks; shuttle is intentionally minimal to avoid coupling with transport layers while enabling safe resume points for long-running generators. Checklist: - Implement core hydrator + tests; - Implement shuttle and adapters for Py/TS/Go; - Add e2e scenario that simulates token rotation mid-stream; - Update examples and docs; - Add feature-flag gating and a migration guide; - Version bumps and changelogs. Testing and CI: unit test coverage added for hydrator jitter logic and shuttle checkpoint/restore; integration test scenario simulates token rotation during a streaming generation with resumable checkpoints; CI initially hit a flaky integ test (stream-resume-on-token-swap) which was retried and passed; load sanity run on dedicated infra shows no regressions in median latency. Rollout plan: feature disabled by default. Gradually enable for SDK beta channels over two weeks, monitor auth-error rates and stream-resume failure alerts; if stable, enable opt-in by default in next minor release and document best practices for hydrate TTL hints. Migration notes: existing SDK users are unaffected until they opt into the hydrator/shuttle APIs. For teams that already build custom refresh loops we provide a compatibility shim that maps older callbacks to the new hydrator interface. Docs: new doc page docs/sdk-auth-hydrator.md with examples in py/ts/go and a short troubleshooting appendix. Complexity: added a small background refresh scheduler per SDK instance; we limited default concurrency and added metrics so ops teams can tune it. Performance: measured small memory increase (~1.6MB per SDK client) and reduced surge of token-refresh calls by ~58% in synthetic rotation tests. Future work: instrument hydrator telemetry into Console, expose server-side hints for prewarming delegated credentials, and explore server-driven checkpoints for stream-shuttle. Related: ENG-4532 tracks further ergonomics and telemetry; SUP-1987 is the customer case that motivated resilient mid-stream token rotation handling.

additional_context: Customer SUP-1987 reported mid-stream token rotations causing opaque stream failures; this change reduces those errors by centralizing refresh and offering resumable checkpoints. We coordinated with support to run the reproduction harness against this branch during validation.
